content:
Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently delivered a talk at the Startup School 2026 event, and the video of her presentation has now been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel. You can watch it below.

Susan Kare shared many wonderful stories and design insights.

More than 40 years have passed since the original Macintosh was launched, yet its graphic design, fonts, icons and overall UI elements still retain that distinctive visual style from back then.

In fact, many of the original concepts Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh still appear in macOS today, whether in spirit or in their original form. From the Command key symbol, the Happy Mac startup icon, the system font, the arrow cursor and more, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac, but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone interested in Apple's history has likely seen Kare's sketches, and has even read or heard her interviews about her early work, being able to hear her talk in person about the passion and frustrations of that era is always a treat — a time when graphical user interfaces and bitmap graphics were still largely uncharted territory.

So, if you are interested in design, in Apple's history, and want to hear someone share their lifelong passion with professional expertise, Kare's talk is definitely a great pleasure to watch.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple, Kare also talked about how she joined the company, showed her work after she left, and shared anecdotes from Apple's early days, as well as quoting other legendary designers for extra inspiration.
